question_text: In which direction does heat flow naturally? / उष्मा (Heat) स्वाभाविक रूप से किस दिशा (Direction) में प्रवाहित (Flow) होती है?
answer: From a hotter object to a colder object / एक गर्म (Hot) वस्तु (Object) से ठंडी (Cold) वस्तु की ओर
options: From a colder object to a hotter object / एक ठंडी (Cold) वस्तु से गर्म (Hot) वस्तु की ओर
From a hotter object to a colder object / एक गर्म (Hot) वस्तु (Object) से ठंडी (Cold) वस्तु की ओर
In both directions equally / दोनों दिशाओं (Directions) में समान रूप से
Heat does not flow / उष्मा (Heat) प्रवाहित (Flow) नहीं होती है
explanation: Heat always flows from a body at a higher temperature to a body at a lower temperature until both reach the same temperature. / उष्मा (Heat) हमेशा उच्च तापमान (High Temperature) वाली वस्तु से कम तापमान (Low Temperature) वाली वस्तु की ओर प्रवाहित (Flow) होती है जब तक कि दोनों का तापमान समान न हो जाए।
distractor_rationale: Option A is a common misconception; cold does not flow, only heat energy flows. Option C is incorrect because net flow is directional. Option D is incorrect as heat is a form of energy in transit.

ai_context.learning_goal: Understand the natural direction of heat transfer.
common_misconceptions: Students often think 'coldness' flows from ice into warm objects.
ai_context.hint: Think about water flowing from a higher level to a lower level.

question_text: Which device is used to measure the temperature of the human body? / मानव (Human) शरीर (Body) का तापमान (Temperature) मापने के लिए किस उपकरण (Device) का उपयोग किया जाता है?
options: Laboratory thermometer / प्रयोगशाला (Laboratory) थर्मामीटर (Thermometer)
Clinical thermometer / क्लिनिकल (Clinical) थर्मामीटर (Thermometer)
Barometer / बैरोमीटर (Barometer)
Anemometer / एनीमोमीटर (Anemometer)
explanation: A clinical thermometer is specifically designed to measure human body temperature, typically ranging from 35°C to 42°C. / क्लिनिकल (Clinical) थर्मामीटर विशेष रूप से मानव (Human) शरीर का तापमान (Temperature) मापने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है।
distractor_rationale: Laboratory thermometers have a wider range and no kink, making them unsuitable for body temperature. Barometers measure pressure, and anemometers measure wind speed.

ai_context.learning_goal: Identify the correct instrument for measuring human body temperature.
common_misconceptions: Confusing laboratory thermometer with a clinical thermometer.
ai_context.hint: This thermometer has a small 'kink' near the bulb to prevent mercury from falling immediately.

question_text: Why are the handles of cooking utensils usually made of plastic or wood? / खाना पकाने के बर्तनों (Utensils) के हैंडल (Handles) आमतौर पर प्लास्टिक (Plastic) या लकड़ी (Wood) के क्यों बने होते हैं?
answer: They are poor conductors of heat / वे उष्मा (Heat) के कुचालक (Poor conductors) होते हैं
options: They are good conductors of heat / वे उष्मा (Heat) के सुचालक (Good conductors) होते हैं
They are poor conductors of heat / वे उष्मा (Heat) के कुचालक (Poor conductors) होते हैं
They look attractive / वे आकर्षक (Attractive) दिखते हैं
They melt easily / वे आसानी से पिघल (Melt) जाते हैं
explanation: Plastic and wood are insulators (poor conductors), so they do not allow heat from the pan to transfer to our hands, preventing burns. / प्लास्टिक और लकड़ी कुचालक (Insulators) हैं, इसलिए वे बर्तन से हमारे हाथों तक उष्मा (Heat) नहीं पहुंचने देते।
distractor_rationale: If they were good conductors (Option A), our hands would burn. Options C and D are irrelevant or incorrect for cooking purposes.

ai_context.learning_goal: Apply the concept of conductors and insulators to everyday objects.
common_misconceptions: Thinking that all parts of a utensil need to get hot for cooking.
ai_context.hint: Think about what would happen to your hand if the handle was made of metal.

question_text: In coastal areas, during the day, the air above the land becomes hot and rises, and cooler air from the sea moves in. What is this phenomenon called? / तटीय (Coastal) क्षेत्रों में, दिन के दौरान भूमि (Land) के ऊपर की हवा गर्म होकर ऊपर उठती है और समुद्र (Sea) से ठंडी हवा अंदर आती है। इस घटना (Phenomenon) को क्या कहा जाता है?
options: Land breeze / भूमि की हवा (Land breeze)
Sea breeze / समुद्री हवा (Sea breeze)
Radiation / विकिरण (Radiation)
Conduction / चालन (Conduction)
explanation: During the day, land heats up faster than water. The hot air above the land rises, and cooler air from the sea rushes in to take its place, creating a sea breeze due to convection. / दिन में, भूमि पानी की तुलना में तेजी से गर्म होती है, जिससे संवहन (Convection) के कारण समुद्री हवा (Sea breeze) उत्पन्न होती है।
distractor_rationale: Land breeze happens at night when the reverse occurs. Conduction and radiation are different modes of heat transfer.

common_misconceptions: Confusing sea breeze with land breeze. Remembering which heats up faster: land or water.
ai_context.hint: The breeze is named after where it comes FROM. It comes from the sea.

question_text: How does the heat from the Sun reach the Earth? / सूर्य की उष्मा (Heat) पृथ्वी (Earth) तक कैसे पहुँचती है?
options: By conduction / चालन (Conduction) द्वारा
By convection / संवहन (Convection) द्वारा
By radiation / विकिरण (Radiation) द्वारा
By both conduction and convection / चालन (Conduction) और संवहन (Convection) दोनों द्वारा
explanation: Space is mostly a vacuum. Radiation is the only method of heat transfer that does not require a medium to travel. / अंतरिक्ष (Space) में कोई माध्यम (Medium) नहीं है। विकिरण (Radiation) ही उष्मा (Heat) स्थानांतरण का एकमात्र तरीका है जिसे माध्यम की आवश्यकता नहीं होती।
distractor_rationale: Conduction requires physical contact between solids. Convection requires a fluid medium (liquid or gas). Since space is a vacuum, only radiation works.

ai_context.learning_goal: Identify radiation as the mode of heat transfer across a vacuum.
common_misconceptions: Thinking that heat travels through the air in space.
ai_context.hint: Remember that there is no air in space. Which mode of heat transfer works without any medium?
